description:
Surfaced 2026-05-08 by POLYBIUS during ariadne--m5e arc. Distillation of agents/design/ariadne--m5e/post-mortem-daedalus-rev3-stall.md §3.3 + §3.4.

## Problem class

Sub-agents (CAPTAINs) occasionally stall mid-dispatch — recon loops on too-large input, output-side context saturation, platform-side streaming hangs. Today's m5e arc had 6+ DAEDALUS rev3 stalls + at least one PLINY orchestrator-level stall + one platform-side session loss. Stalls are detectable post-hoc but the substrate has no in-flight recovery discipline.

## Two related items

### Item 1: Sub-agent watchdog (post-mortem §3.3)

When PLINY dispatches a sub-agent (CAPTAIN), the agent should be watchdog-killed if it hits an empirical stall signature without producing a deliverable Write/Edit. Empirical signature from today's m5e stalls (DAEDALUS reading rev2 at ~31k tokens, re-reading 4 times, never reaching Write):

- Token budget threshold: > 50k tokens consumed
- Tool use threshold: > 20 tool calls executed
- Critical predicate: NO Write/Edit on the deliverable path

If all three hold, kill the agent and surface to PLINY/POLYBIUS for routing.

Implementation surface lives in MAJOR_PLINY.md as a dispatch-protocol addition: PLINY monitors sub-agent telemetry (whatever Claude Code surfaces), enforces the threshold, kills + surfaces on trip.

Open question for design: how does PLINY actually monitor sub-agent telemetry from the parent session? May require periodic polling or platform-side hooks. If the platform doesn't expose token/tool-use counts to the parent, the watchdog reduces to wall-clock heuristic only.

### Item 2: JSONL transcript save before kill (post-mortem §3.4)

Whenever a sub-agent is killed (watchdog or manual), capture the JSONL transcript of the dispatch BEFORE the process exits. Today's stalls left no diagnostic trace — the post-mortem had to reconstruct from screenshots and intermittent status snapshots. JSONL transcript is the only direct evidence of what the agent was doing at stall time.

Save target: `.claude/diagnostics/<agent>-<dispatch-id>-<timestamp>.jsonl` or similar.

Read-side discipline: when post-mortem authoring, the JSONL transcripts are first-line evidence; reconstruction-from-memory is fallback only.

## Scope

- MAJOR_PLINY.md substrate edit defining the watchdog protocol + thresholds
- operating-disciplines.md (or substrate equivalent) defining the JSONL-save discipline
- Possibly a new helper script if Claude Code doesn't expose the telemetry/transcript natively

## Gauntlet

DAEDALUS-light (substrate design — small but architecturally meaningful since it touches the dispatch protocol) + ADA + CATO. Can skip ARGUS unless DAEDALUS surfaces real architectural risk.

## Out of scope

- Orchestrator-level (PLINY) self-checkpoint discipline — that's a separate substrate concern (see stoa--... pending; orchestrator session forking after N tickets / M tokens).
- Watchdog for non-CAPTAIN sub-agents (Explore, general-purpose, etc.).

## Empirical anchor
